methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a Norfolk native directly build distributed, grassroots AI literacy in a non-metro region, demonstrating peer-to-peer knowledge transfer that could break concentration patterns if sustained and replicated.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: A college-led WorkAI Lab signals institutional capacity-building in a mid-tier region, but its concentration within higher education may deepen capability gaps between credential-holders and surrounding communities rather than distributing fluency broadly.

signals.title: Roanoke County Public Schools prepare to update AI policy - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: School policy updates around AI indicate platform-mediated adoption through institutional channels—likely shallow integration as students use existing AI tools rather than building deep technical capability, but reaching beyond traditional tech hubs.

signals.title: After severe 76% electricity price hikes due to AI data centers, Virginia requires firms to pay for all dedicated upstream electrical infrastructure — state regulators crack down, governor says move will save civilians ‘hundreds of millions of dollars’ - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Electricity price hikes of 76% from data center expansion impose economic externalities on residents statewide while AI capability remains concentrated in corporate hands, materializing neither deep public fluency nor equitable distribution of benefits.

signals.title: West Virginia begins rollout of first-in-the-nation AI literacy and digital science curriculum - Tri-State Alert
signals.signal_reading: West Virginia's first-in-nation AI literacy curriculum creates competitive pressure and potential knowledge spillover into neighboring Southwest Virginia, signaling that systematic K-12 education policy could enable distributed deep fluency across rural Appalachian regions.
